input: Enroll in a home barista espresso technique course

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Espresso technique courses range from beginner fundamentals (dialing in grind, tamping) to advanced skills (latte art, milk texturing, extraction science) — knowing the depth changes which course fits.
The user may prefer an in-person local class, a live online session, or a self-paced video course — this completely changes where to look and what to enroll in.
The course could be for the user alone, a partner, or a gift for someone else — affects enrollment count, scheduling flexibility, and whether gifting options matter.
Course prices vary widely from free YouTube content to $300+ structured programs — a budget ceiling narrows the options significantly.
The user's current home equipment (espresso machine, grinder, etc.) determines whether a course is immediately practical or requires gear acquisition first.
Some learners want a structured curriculum with certification; others prefer a casual, community-style learning experience — this shapes which platform or provider to prioritize.

The end goal could be making a great daily espresso at home, hosting guests confidently, or reaching near-professional skill — this defines what 'done well' looks like and which course depth is right.

gold.taskTitle: Enroll in a home barista espresso course
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to find and enroll in a course that teaches espresso-making techniques suited to a home barista context.

questions.title: What is your current espresso skill level?
questions.description: Is the user a complete beginner, someone who owns a machine but struggles with consistency, or already comfortable with basics and looking to refine technique?

questions.title: Do you prefer in-person, live online, or self-paced?
questions.description: Determines whether to search for local coffee schools, scheduled virtual classes, or on-demand platforms like Skillshare or dedicated barista course sites.

questions.title: Is this course just for you or others too?
questions.description: Clarifies whether the user needs a single enrollment, multiple seats, or a giftable format.

questions.title: What is your budget for this course?
questions.description: A clear price ceiling helps filter out free resources vs. mid-range structured courses vs. premium or certification programs.

questions.title: What espresso equipment do you already own at home?
questions.description: Knowing whether the user has a machine, a grinder, or neither determines if the course content will be immediately applicable or if gear gaps need addressing first.

questions.title: Do you want a structured curriculum or a casual learning style?
questions.description: Some users want a step-by-step syllabus with progress tracking or a certificate; others prefer informal tips, community forums, and flexible modules.

questions.title: What specific outcome matters most to you after the course?
questions.description: For example: consistently pulling a great shot daily, mastering milk steaming for lattes, understanding extraction science, or impressing guests — defines which course focus delivers the most value.
